formation.text: The early graph is described as a person with two or four flanking marks. This supports a picture-based account, but does not settle whether the marks depict or indicate anything, or what the whole graph originally meant. The received 說文 analysis divides it into 八 and 人; that later analysis does not prove the original construction.

components.text: Early-form descriptions identify a human figure corresponding to 人, though they do not establish that it was a separate component in the original graph. The received 說文 analysis later identifies 人 as one part.

The early form is described with flanking dots. Their identity and role are disputed: proposals treat them as marks for “between,” armor or covering, secondary status, or ritual sparks. Their identification with modern 丶 is tentative.

history.text: Early forms are described as a person flanked by two or four marks; the reports do not establish a sequence among these forms.
In clerical script, the following component was regularized as 人. The side form 亻 is also recorded as a variant. This later graphic history does not settle the character’s earliest construction.

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.field: 形義通解；甲骨文、說文、早期用例及異說
evidence.text: The database describes oracle-bone forms as 人 with two or four dots flanking the figure, and reports an interpretation as “between” attributed to Yang Shuda and Shen Pei. It cites 左傳·襄公九年 and 左傳·襄公三十年 for 介居/介於 between two great states. It also records disputed readings: an armor/clothing interpretation (Luo Zhenyu, Wang Guowei, Ma Xulun), oracle-bone 介 meaning ‘junior/secondary’ (Rao Zongyi, Qiu Xigui, Wu Shichang), and Warring States slips using 介 for 個 (‘one item/person’). The database gives the Shuowen account 畫也。从八从人，人各有介, but this is an early lexicographic analysis, not independent confirmation of the graph’s origin.
evidence.kind: dictionary account and reported scholarly interpretations
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.field: 甲骨文字形考释 and proposed semantic development
evidence.text: Xu describes the oracle-bone shape as a person with dots at both sides (some variants have two dots on each side). He surveys armor, shell/scale, between, human hair, and 個-related accounts, and argues that the dots are sparks from a person burned in a rain-making ritual, with the person acting as intermediary between humans and heaven; he proposes ‘intermediary’ as the original lexical sense. This is the author’s argued hypothesis, not settled evidence: the article itself notes that the dot component’s meaning and the graph’s original semantic construction remain disputed.
evidence.kind: secondary scholarly proposal and review of competing analyses
evidence.title: 徐山：释“介”

evidence.source: ShuoWen.org, citing 段玉裁《說文解字注》
evidence.field: 說文解字注, 畫 entry
evidence.text: The page gives Duan Yucai’s note that 介 and 畍 are old/new forms in the relation to ‘boundary’; dividing/separating necessarily entails an interval, so 介 extended to ‘between/interval.’ This is Qing-period commentary on the received Shuowen text, not an ancient dated attestation of the semantic development.
evidence.title: 說文解字「畫」

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 研訂說明; 形體資料表
evidence.text: The entry quotes the Shuowen analysis and explains a later graphic development: the component following 介 was regularized as 人 in clerical script, yielding 介, and in a side-component position as 亻, producing a recorded variant. It names Han stele and Dunhuang sources for that variant, but the page does not expose oracle-bone or bronze form images in its public form table. Thus it supports the clerical-form account, not a reconstruction of the earliest graph.
evidence.title: [A00076-002] 介 – Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Chinese Text Project dictionary, entry 个
evidence.text: The entry labels 个 a variant of 個 and gives Guangyun’s gloss for a side chamber of the Ming Hall. Its Kangxi quotation lists older textual examples of 个 for an individual/counting unit and says 个 and 介 can be interchangeable in some citations, including 一介臣/一个臣 and 一介行李/一个. These are dictionary citations of classical texts; they do not establish that 介 originated as a phonetic component or prove the direction/date of borrowing. The source also identifies 个 as a semantic variant of 個.
evidence.title: 个 – Chinese Text Project

evidence.source: Local Baxter–Sagart TSV, checked against official Unicode Unihan pages (the official pages could not be opened)
evidence.field: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv row 1686 (介); rows 1033–1034 (個, 个); current Mandarin readings corroborated by opened Unicode property mirrors
evidence.text: The local dataset gives 介 Mandarin jiè, Middle Chinese keajH, Old Chinese *kˤr[e]p-s; it gives 個 and 个 Mandarin gè, Middle Chinese kaH, Old Chinese *kˤa[r]-s. This is a real Baxter–Sagart contrast in the checked rows, not a single matching reconstructed form. Current kMandarin values are jiè for 介 and gè for 个/個; Unicode GetUnihanData pages were attempted but inaccessible through the browser, so the official records cannot serve as verified click-through evidence here. No phonetic-component claim is made for 介.

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

The meaning of the flanking dots is unresolved: ‘between,’ armor/covering, secondary status, and Xu Shan’s sparks/ritual-intermediary proposal conflict. Component roles beyond 人 plus nonidentified marks are not securely established; neither 人 nor 八 should be assigned an independently proven semantic/phonetic role from the received Shuowen account alone.

The database reports oracle-bone usages, including ‘junior/secondary’ and a proposed ‘seek’ reading, but this research did not inspect the underlying inscription facsimiles or primary corpus entries. Their dates and readings remain to be independently verified.
Later senses such as shell/scale, armor, assist, introduce, and intermediary are not all linked by dated evidence in the inspected sources. Do not infer a chronology from the dossier’s gloss list.

A Warring States bamboo-slip use of 介 for 個 is reported by the CUHK database, while Wiktionary’s dossier excerpt says 個／个 usage is attested since Song. The source packet conflates graphic/sense history; the exact early slip transcription, date, and relationship between whole-graph borrowing and later 個/个 forms need primary edition verification.

The exact Unicode Unihan records for U+4ECB, U+4E2A, and U+500B were inaccessible. Current Mandarin readings were corroborated only through nonofficial mirrors for the relevant characters; official click-through citations remain unverified.

Baxter–Sagart rows differ: 介 *kˤr[e]p-s vs 個/个 *kˤa[r]-s, with MC keajH vs kaH. No phonetic-component/loan analysis is supported by the inspected sources, and matching current gè/jiè-like readings cannot establish an ancient sound relation.
